# Captain Claw

> A fictional gaming platform — store, library, friends and party sessions —
> built for the WebMCP Challenge. It registers 14 WebMCP tools on
> `document.modelContext`, so a browser agent can read what the player is
> currently looking at, change what is on their screen, search the catalog,
> create a party and send invitations. Users, libraries and game data are
> synthetic. No real game is launched.

Captain Claw is agent-operable at runtime, not merely agent-readable. In a
WebMCP-capable browser, prefer the registered tools over reading the DOM: they
return structured JSON and they act on the same state the player sees. Tools
that only read are annotated `readOnlyHint`. Everything an agent can do here is
also possible through the normal UI.

Searching is not the same as showing. `search_games` and the library tools only
read — they leave the player's screen exactly as it was. Once you have decided
what to recommend, call `show_games` with those ids (or `apply_filters` when
your answer really is a filter) so the player ends up looking at the games you
are describing. Both work from any page and will move the player to the Store
if they are somewhere without a filter bar.

## Pages

- [Home](https://captainclaw.netlify.app/): entry point and featured games.
- [Store](https://captainclaw.netlify.app/store): full catalog, with search and genre, player-count, co-op and session-length filters.
- [Library](https://captainclaw.netlify.app/library): the signed-in player's owned games, with playtime, completion and install state.
- [Friends](https://captainclaw.netlify.app/friends): friends with presence and what each is playing right now.
- [Party](https://captainclaw.netlify.app/party): the current party, its invitations and whether it is ready to launch.

## WebMCP tools

- [Read tools](https://github.com/PurpleWizard07/captain-claw/blob/master/src/webmcp/readTools.tsx): `get_online_friends`, `get_my_library`, `get_friend_libraries`, `search_games`, `get_game_details`. Registered on every page.
- [View tools](https://github.com/PurpleWizard07/captain-claw/blob/master/src/webmcp/viewTools.tsx): `get_current_view`, `apply_filters`, `show_games` and `open_game`. Registered on every page; the two that need a filter bar navigate to the Store when the player is not on one.
- [Party tools](https://github.com/PurpleWizard07/captain-claw/blob/master/src/webmcp/partyTools.tsx): `create_party`, `invite_friends`, `get_party_status`, `launch_session`. `respond_to_invite` is registered only while the signed-in player has an invitation pending.
- [Registration hook](https://github.com/PurpleWizard07/captain-claw/blob/master/src/webmcp/useTool.ts): how tools are registered, torn down with `AbortController`, and how errors are returned as structured data rather than opaque failures.

## Optional

- [README](https://github.com/PurpleWizard07/captain-claw/blob/master/README.md): full project write-up, architecture and verification suite.
- [Session-length rule](https://github.com/PurpleWizard07/captain-claw/blob/master/src/lib/filterGames.ts): `maxSessionMinutes` is a budget, not a hard cutoff — a game fits when its shortest session is within budget and its longest exceeds it by no more than 30%.
- [Evals](https://github.com/PurpleWizard07/captain-claw/blob/master/evals/webmcp-evals.json): the scripted agent scenarios used to check the tools.
